subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or should cron keep `status=ok` and surface delivery failure through delivery-specific fields and warning UI?
rationale: Both models are represented by open PRs and the choice changes persisted status, Gateway schema, Control UI rendering, backoff behavior, and external consumer semantics.

options.title: Approve ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Land the narrower contract where execution remains `ok` and operators use `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered successful runs.

options.title: Adopt first-class warning
options.body: Use the broader warning-status model only after updating storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and compatibility proof across repo-owned clients.

options.title: Keep delivery failures as errors
options.body: Reject the split for now so post-run delivery failures continue to drive `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Approve ok plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Land the narrower contract where execution remains `ok` and operators use `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered successful runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current status/finalizer lines and recent cron outcome history point to this owner for the cross-surface cron semantics choice.
